abstract: We introduce LongBanana, to our knowledge the first expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for long-context multi-reference image synthesis in the age of agent-driven image generation. The task requires retrieving dispersed visual evidence, rejecting distractors, binding entities and relations, and composing one coherent final image from multiple references. LongBanana contains 90 carefully designed tasks organized by a 3-by-3 taxonomy; each task includes about 32 reference images, 20 constraints, and 50 evaluation items, yielding 4,670 expert-specified atomic evaluation items in total. Its graph-grounded evaluation design instantiates each task with reference images and an entity–relation graph, then converts node, edge, and whole-graph obligations into checklist items for Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction. Reviewed expert labels include a 15% double-labeled subset with 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa. We further introduce LongBanana-Gen, an agent-harness framework for long-horizon image generation; experiments show that minimal agent harnesses improve over direct generation, while a ReAct–Plan–Exec–Reflect (RPR) workflow yields harness-dependent gains by strengthening evidence grounding and repair. Together, LongBanana provides an auditable testbed for measuring dense visual evidence use and a shared target for developing stronger agent-driven image-generation systems. Code and data are available at the project page: https://long-banana.com/.

sections.body: The paper argues that a realistic image can still be wrong: it may use the wrong reference, bind a style to the wrong object, or break a count, and a holistic score misses these failures. Each task is modeled as an entity–relation graph, and the graph is scored through atomic checklist items under Content Fidelity, Relational Binding, and Global Constraint Satisfaction. The scorer, LongBananaEval, routes items to rubric critics and calls tools for OCR, counting, layout, and identity checks. On 900 audited outputs with 46,700 reviewed labels, a 15% double-labeled subset reaches 89.4% exact agreement and 0.83 quadratic weighted kappa. The authors also report that no single agent harness dominates the per-subclass scores.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Multi-reference image generation errors are provenance failures that holistic realism scores cannot localize.

sections.body: Each case gives a system a heterogeneous reference set and a structured synthesis instruction, and asks for one image that satisfies its entity–relation graph. The benchmark has 90 cases, with 10 in each of nine subclasses across three suites. A typical case has approximately 32 references and more than 20 cross-reference constraints, and experts specify 4,670 atomic checklist items in total. Experts write scenarios, an LLM structures each one into nodes, edges, and whole-graph constraints, and that graph guides the instruction and references. At least 30 cases include two or more hard-negative references. Human curators check references, visual feasibility, and item verifiability before a case is included.
sections.heading: The LongBanana Benchmark
sections.headline: LongBanana contains 90 cases across a 3-by-3 taxonomy, each scored through atomic graph-derived checklist items.

sections.body:
The held-out 90-case benchmark is used for judge validation and generation comparisons.

- **Judge agreement:** LongBananaEval reaches Pearson 0.8707 and Kendall 0.6727 against reviewed expert overall scores, versus 0.8413 and 0.6437 for a single-pass VLM-as-judge baseline.
- **Strategies with Nano Banana 2:** full-prompt direct generation scores 68.4 overall, prompt-decomposed direct generation scores 74.6, and OpenClaw with RPR scores 78.4.
- **Backends under OpenClaw + RPR:** Seedream 4 scores 63.6 and GPT Image 1 scores 61.8, and Nano Banana 2 leads across all nine subclasses.
- **Limits:** RPR gains depend on the harness. Hermes-Agent rises from 73.9 to 75.6 with RPR, while OpenCode rises from 77.3 to 77.8.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Nano Banana 2 under OpenClaw with RPR scores 78.4 overall, above the 68.4 of full-prompt direct generation.

sections.body: The benchmark has 90 expert-designed and expert-verified cases across the 3-by-3 taxonomy, with 4,670 atomic checklist items. Its scorer turns constraints into evidence-linked judgments that are validated against human labels. The generation study contrasts PD-Direct, which has privileged access to the construction graph and an exactly optimized staging schedule, with agentic workflows. PD-Direct is a competitive non-agentic baseline. Agentic workflows reach broader success without access to that graph, which the authors attribute to adaptive evidence use and generation control. The RPR component study supports coordinating retrieval, execution, and repair within one workflow. The authors propose agents that reason over both task structure and the evolving visual state.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Agentic workflows reach broader success than a fixed privileged schedule, and checklist scores localize failures.

sections.body:
- **A: Related work** covers image-synthesis benchmarks, atomic constraint evaluation, and automatic judges.
- **B: Benchmark details** gives the taxonomy, construction steps, statistics, provenance, the evaluation schema, and label quality control, which reports 0 schema validation errors.
- **C: LongBananaEval details** covers model declarations, judge–human agreement, and difficulty-weighted scoring.
- **D: Further experiments** includes the workflow ablation and case-paired diagnostics. OpenClaw + RPR is 2.3 pp above minimal OpenClaw, with interval [+0.6, +4.2] pp.
- **E: Release safeguards** states limitations: the taxonomy excludes video generation and 3D scene composition, and scorer results depend on backbone models and tool versions.
